attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, writable), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10. Built a dedicated cluster CA on node1, issued per-node server certs (CN/SAN matching each host) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator), distributed via SSH to all nodes into /var/lib/pgsql/tls (outside the data directory so it survives pg_basebackup copies). Enabled ssl on all nodes, and restricted pg_hba.conf on the primary to hostssl-only replication connections requiring a client certificate signed by the cluster CA (auth method 'cert', explicit hostnossl reject for the replication pseudo-db). Verified negative case (no client cert -> rejected) and positive case (valid CA-issued cert -> accepted) before building real standbys via pg_basebackup -R, which auto-populated primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and the replicator cert/key. Confirmed streaming replication and data propagation end-to-end. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baselines, restarted node2, node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until each came back, proved boot_id changed on all three, and confirmed post-restart recovery — postgresql active, correct pg_is_in_recovery() state, TLS+cert replication reconnected (pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl showing ssl=t, client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standbys), primary writable again, and a post-restart write replicated to both standbys.
